chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever frequently remembers Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Allah will love him; and whoever frequently remembers Allah, two acquittals are written for him: an acquittal from the Fire and an acquittal from hypocrisy.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards of frequently remembering Allah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of the Ahl al-Bayt in al-Kafi, underscores dhikr as a transformative practice that secures divine love and dual deliverance from the Hellfire and hypocrisy. In Shia scholarship, this 'freedom from hypocrisy' is often interpreted not merely as absence of doubt, but as the preservation of sincere faith amidst worldly trials, linking the believer's inner state to their ultimate salvation.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washha, from Dawood Bin Sirhan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The one who frequently mentions (Zikr) of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic, Allahazwj would Love him, and the one who frequently mentions (Zikr) Allahazwj, two requittals are Written for him – a requital from the Fire and a requital from the hypocrisy’.
en.sarwar: 3. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad and A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from al- Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from Dawud ibn Serhan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Whoever speaks of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, often Allah loves him and whoever speaks of Allah very often, two kinds of freedoms will be written for him: freedom from fire and freedom from hypocrisy.’”
